cases.description: Microsoft's documented example: the equivalent interest rate for 10,000 growing to 11,000 over 96 months
cases.expected_note: Excel documents this example's result as 0.0009933 (0.09933% per month). Derived from the documented formula RRI = (fv/pv)^(1/nper) - 1 = 1.1^(1/96) - 1 = 0.00099331

cases.description: A clean closed-form case: quadrupling in two periods is exactly 100% per period
cases.expected_note: (400/100)^(1/2) - 1 = 2 - 1 = 1 exactly, i.e. a 100% return each period

cases.description: A future value below the present value gives a negative equivalent rate
Zero periods makes the exponent 1/nper undefined
cases.expected_note: Excel documents #NUM! if nper is less than or equal to 0 (and if pv is less than or equal to 0)

cases.description: A present value of zero makes the fv/pv ratio undefined
cases.expected_note: Excel documents #NUM! if pv is less than or equal to 0
